subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: Should this iMessage repair rewrite the sender only after canonical handle normalization, and should unrepaired local-sender direct messages fail closed before access control?
rationale: The repaired sender becomes the iMessage policy subject, pairing id, route key, and reply target, so accepting a weaker comparison or an unrepairable fallback is a security-boundary choice rather than routine cleanup.

options.title: Require Canonical Repair And Proof
options.body: Fix peer selection to use normalizeIMessageHandle, add coverage for formatted or service-prefixed local handles, and require redacted after-fix live proof before merge.

options.title: Accept Source-Only Identity Risk
options.body: Maintainers could merge based on source review plus pre-fix incident evidence while owning the remaining live-payload and candidate-selection uncertainty.

options.title: Pause For Narrower Root Cause
options.body: If the author's current failure is a different iMessage issue, pause or close this branch and track the root cause in a narrower follow-up.

recommendation.title: Require Canonical Repair And Proof
recommendation.body: Fix peer selection to use normalizeIMessageHandle, add coverage for formatted or service-prefixed local handles, and require redacted after-fix live proof before merge.
